sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page ndom1244 (references and MED: Johnston 1919 'wordlist_or_less'; classification comment citing Elderkin 2003:583, Vansina 2004:273-283)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms no grammar, sketch or phonology is registered for Ndombe.

sources.citation: Jordan, Linda. 2015. A Comparison of Five Speech Varieties of Southwestern Angola: Comparing OluHumbe, OluCilenge, OluKwandu, OluNgendelengo, and OluKuvale in the Kamucuio Municipality, Namibe Province. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2015-017.
sources.note: Ndombe language not covered ('Ndombe Grande' appears only as a place name); explicitly says 'Tone is not covered in this paper'; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Gomes, Armindo Jaime. 2014. Mundombe do «Dombe» ou Ndombe do Mundombe?... Mulemba: Revista Angolana de Ciências Sociais 4(8): 77-100. DOI 10.4000/mulemba.401 (CORE/OpenEdition PDF)
sources.note: Nothing; onomastics/identity paper. States the Vandombe of Dombe Grande today mostly speak Umbundu, with olundombe surviving residually in family contexts, and that colonial authors treated olundombe as a cross between Umbundu and Olucilenge.

sources.citation: Elderkin, Edward D. 2003. Herero. In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, p. 583 (Routledge) — checked in on-disk text of the volume
sources.note: Page concerns zone R subgrouping (Nkumbi, Wambo, Herero, Umbundu); Ndombe appears in the volume only in the Guthrie/Maho code list (R12); nothing on Ndombe prosody.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Group X, South-West Africa languages, phonology/prefix commentary)
sources.note: Group X commentary mentions Ndombe (no. 93) only for the class 6 prefix Ba-; no statement on stress or accent for Ndombe.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Ndombe = language no. 93, pp. 350-351 footnote, p. 780 supplementary vocabulary, pp. 800-801 bibliography note)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives only 8 Ndombe words (p. 780) and calls it a 'scarcely known tongue' / 'as yet scarcely illustrated' (p. 800-801); his 'Ndombe or Kwando, 93a Koroka' is placed on the Mossamedes coast and said to be 'very similar to Olunyaneka'.

sources.citation: Ferreira Diniz, José de Oliveira. 1918. Populações indígenas de Angola. Coimbra: Imprensa da Universidade. ('Mondombes', pp. 371-374)
sources.note: Nothing; the Mondombe section (coast south of Benguela, Coporolo basin) is purely ethnographic, with no language subsection.

sources.citation: Vansina, Jan. 2004. How Societies Are Born: Governance in West Central Africa before 1600. Charlottesville: University of Virginia Press, pp. 273-283 (appendix on Njila languages).

sources.note: Cited by Glottolog for Ndombe's subclassification; classificatory only, unlikely to mention accent, but confirms what data exist.
